nodes.content: Design distributed training recovery that preserves optimizer and data progress consistency across failures and worker membership changes.
requirements: Recovered executions match failure-free optimizer-update and sample-consumption histories, including failures during resharding.
Recovery adds at most 5% failure-free step latency versus identical training without recovery support.

nodes.content: Use deterministic step-indexed sampling, asynchronous copy-on-write optimizer/cursor snapshots, and atomic epoch-fenced manifests for replay-safe resharding.
How should epoch-fenced manifests atomically commit optimizer state, sampling position, and shard ownership when a worker fails mid-reshard?
An epoch-fenced manifest atomically referencing durable optimizer snapshots, sample cursors, and shard maps enables deterministic replay after mid-reshard failures.
Durably stage optimizer/cursor snapshots and shard maps, CAS-publish epoch-fenced manifests, then test mid-reshard replay and ≤5% step-latency overhead.
Inject 200 mid-reshard crashes during 8-to-12-worker ReshardBench transitions; compare optimizer/sample traces against uninterrupted runs and latency against recovery-disabled training.
ReshardBench: all 200 mid-reshard recoveries matched uninterrupted optimizer-update and sample-consumption traces; recovery-enabled median step latency rose 3.2%.
Run ManifestRace with 500 crashes around concurrent epoch-fenced CAS publications; compare replay traces and p95 latency against recovery-disabled runs.
ManifestRace: 9/500 crash trials duplicated sample IDs when stale-epoch workers continued after manifest CAS; p95 latency overhead was 6.1%.
Epoch-fenced per-step optimizer/cursor commits reject stale workers; batched lease checks preserve exact replay with p95 overhead ≤5%.
Implement epoch-checked step commits binding optimizer/cursor snapshots to shard maps; batch worker lease checks, then rerun ManifestRace and p95 benchmarks.
Rerun 500 ManifestRace CAS-adjacent crashes comparing original manifests with epoch-checked commits and batched leases; measure duplicates and p95 overhead.
With failed workers terminated before CAS, original manifests matched 500/500 traces; per-step commits also matched 500/500 with continuing workers.
ManifestRace: per-step commits preserved exact traces, but batched lease checks raised p95 step latency 8.4% versus recovery-disabled training.
Run LeasePiggyback with stale-worker injections and epoch checks on gradient all-reduces; measure replay mismatches and p95 latency overhead.
LeasePiggyback: 0/500 stale-worker replay mismatches; piggybacked batched lease checks reduced p95 latency overhead from 8.4% to 4.3%.
Adopt epoch-checked per-step commits with collective-piggybacked leases: standalone checks cost 8.4% p95 overhead versus 4.3% with piggybacking.
Use a quorum-replicated step ledger with deterministic sample ranges, idempotent optimizer commits, and asynchronous compaction across membership changes.
Can quorum-replicated step records bind sample ranges to optimizer commits through resharding without exceeding 5% p95 step overhead?
Quorum-committed step IDs atomically bind sample ranges and optimizer deltas, yielding exact replay with ≤5% p95 latency overhead.
Implement three-replica quorum step records with idempotent optimizer deltas; inject resharding failures and benchmark p95 step overhead against recovery-disabled runs.
Inject 500 LedgerCrash failures during commits, resharding, and compaction; compare optimizer/sample histories and p95 overhead against uninterrupted and recovery-disabled baselines.
LedgerCrash: 6/500 compaction-reshard failures duplicated sample ranges; quorum writes raised p95 step latency 7.2% versus recovery-disabled training.
Run LedgerIsolation with asynchronous compaction enabled versus disabled during 8-to-12-worker resharding; measure duplicate sample ranges and p95 overhead.
LedgerIsolation: pausing asynchronous compaction during resharding eliminated duplicates (0/500 versus 6/500) and lowered p95 overhead to 4.6%.
Adopt the quorum ledger with compaction paused during resharding: duplicate trials fell from 6/500 to 0/500; p95 overhead reached 4.6%.
Maintain shadow optimizer shards and sampler counters on standby workers, fencing reshard handoffs with two-phase ownership transfer.
How do standby shadows distinguish committed optimizer updates from speculative transfers if a worker fails between ownership-transfer phases?
Epoch-tagged shadow optimizer deltas and sampler counters applied only after ownership-commit markers ensure exact replay with ≤5% p95 overhead.
Implement epoch-tagged standby deltas with ownership-commit markers; fault both handoff phases and compare histories and p95 latency against baseline.
Inject 400 ShadowHandoff crashes before and after ownership commits; compare promoted-shadow optimizer/sample traces with uninterrupted runs.
ShadowHandoff trace bundle contains 400 crash logs, ownership-commit markers, promoted-shadow snapshots, and optimizer/sample history comparisons.
Audit ShadowHandoff traces for speculative-delta promotion and replay mismatches; benchmark standby replication’s p95 step overhead against recovery-disabled training.
ShadowHandoff: 400/400 promoted-shadow histories matched uninterrupted runs; zero speculative deltas applied, with 4.8% p95 overhead versus recovery-disabled training.
Retain shadow handoffs as an alternative: 400/400 exact recoveries and 4.8% p95 overhead, pending comparison with ledger and fenced commits.
Replay from incremental checkpoints using seeded global-batch IDs, membership-invariant reductions, and fenced reshard barriers.
Can seeded global-batch replay reproduce optimizer updates across different worker counts when floating-point reduction order changes?
Fixed-order FP32 reduction trees indexed by global-batch IDs yield bitwise-identical optimizer updates across worker counts with ≤5% p95 overhead.
Implement batch-ID-indexed FP32 reductions and checkpoint replay; test 8-to-12-worker failures for bitwise updates and p95 overhead.
Run ReplayTree over 300 checkpoint-to-reshard crashes, comparing bitwise optimizer hashes, sample IDs, and p95 latency to uninterrupted training.
ReplayTree matched optimizer hashes and sample IDs in 300/300 recoveries, but p95 step latency rose 7.6% versus uninterrupted training.
Pipelining batch-ID-fixed reduction-tree chunks preserves bitwise replay across worker counts while reducing p95 step overhead below 5%.
Run PipelinedReplay across 300 reshard crashes; compare optimizer hashes and sample IDs against uninterrupted runs, p95 latency against recovery-disabled training.
PipelinedReplay matched optimizer hashes and sample IDs in 300/300 reshard recoveries; p95 step overhead fell to 4.9%.
Stress PipelinedReplay on mixed-precision 4-to-16-worker transitions with 500 mid-accumulation crashes; compare optimizer hashes, sample IDs, and p95 overhead.
PipelinedReplay mixed-precision: 12/500 mid-accumulation recoveries mismatched optimizer hashes after 4-to-16-worker resharding; sample IDs matched; p95 overhead reached 5.7%.
Fenced microbatch checkpoints of FP32 accumulators and loss-scaler state plus adaptive pipelining restore bitwise replay with ≤5% p95 overhead.
Checkpoint FP32 accumulators and loss-scaler state at fenced microbatch boundaries; tune pipelining, then repeat mixed-precision crashes and p95 benchmarks.
Repeat 500 mixed-precision 4-to-16-worker mid-accumulation crashes with fenced microbatch checkpoints; compare optimizer hashes, sample IDs, and p95 overhead.
FencedMicrobatch matched optimizer hashes and sample IDs in 500/500 mixed-precision recoveries; adaptive pipelining cut p95 step overhead to 4.7%.
Inject 600 checkpoint-publication crashes during 16-to-4-worker resharding; compare optimizer/sample histories against uninterrupted runs and p95 overhead against recovery-disabled runs.
CheckpointPublish: 8/600 16-to-4-worker crashes loaded mixed-generation accumulator shards, changing optimizer hashes; sample IDs matched, p95 overhead 4.8%.
Defer FencedMicrobatch adoption: despite 500/500 exact mid-accumulation recoveries, 8/600 publication crashes mixed accumulator generations; require atomic checkpoint manifests.
Atomic generation manifests for accumulator shards and loss-scaler state prevent mixed-generation restores while preserving bitwise replay and ≤5% p95 overhead.
Durably stage all accumulator shards and scaler state, atomically publish generation manifests, then repeat checkpoint-publication crashes and p95 benchmarking.
Repeat 600 CheckpointPublish crashes during 16-to-4-worker resharding with atomic manifests; check optimizer hashes, sample IDs, and p95 step overhead.
CheckpointPublish with atomic manifests matched optimizer hashes and sample IDs in 600/600 recoveries; p95 step overhead was 4.9%.
Adopt atomic-manifest FencedMicrobatch over unpipelined replay: fixes earlier mismatch modes, passes 600/600 publication crashes, and achieves 4.9% p95 overhead.
Erasure-code optimizer shards and sampler cursors across workers, using joint-consensus epoch barriers to transfer ownership during resharding.
Can joint-consensus epoch barriers reconstruct committed erasure-coded optimizer shards without replaying sample ranges after simultaneous worker loss?
A 6+2 Reed–Solomon stripe committed alongside sampler cursors under joint-consensus epochs recovers two worker losses exactly with ≤5% p95 overhead.
Implement 6+2 coded optimizer/cursor stripes and joint-consensus epoch commits; inject two-worker losses during resharding and benchmark p95 overhead.
Run CodedReshard with 500 paired worker losses across epoch commits; compare reconstructed optimizer/sample traces and p95 latency to baselines.
CodedReshard: 500/500 paired-loss recoveries matched optimizer and sample histories; 6+2 coding added 4.4% p95 step latency.
Stress CodedReshard with 700 paired losses during parity regeneration and 8-to-16-worker transitions; compare histories and p95 overhead.
CodedReshard: 11/700 regeneration-phase losses reconstructed mixed-epoch optimizer shards; p95 step overhead reached 5.6% during 8-to-16-worker transitions.
Generation-fenced parity regeneration with atomic stripe manifests and pipelined encoding prevents mixed-epoch reconstruction under two losses at ≤5% p95 overhead.
Fence parity regeneration by epoch, atomically publish complete stripe manifests, pipeline encoding, then repeat paired-loss trials and p95 benchmarking.
Compare original and generation-fenced 6+2 stripes across 700 parity-regeneration failures; measure optimizer/sample mismatches and p95 step overhead.
Generation-fenced 6+2 stripes cut optimizer/sample-history mismatches from 11/700 to 0/700; pipelined encoding held p95 overhead at 4.8%.
Inject 900 paired losses around stripe-manifest publication during 16-to-8-worker resharding; check committed generations, replay histories, and p95 overhead.
StripePublish: 7/900 paired losses restored mixed-epoch optimizer shards when manifest publication outran parity durability; p95 overhead was 4.9%.
Defer coded recovery: fencing fixed regeneration failures, but 7/900 publication crashes still mixed epochs; require durable parity before manifest CAS.
Choose epoch-checked commits with collective-piggybacked leases: 0/500 replay mismatches, 4.3% p95 overhead; retain ledger, shadows, and replay as alternatives.
